hypotheses.claim: Because the weakest regime reported by the archive is capacity_level=tight (12 instances, vbs_rel_gap_pct = -22.59%) and depot_style=eccentric (-20.35%), the current score_ruin_nodes ranking must be under-serving load-critical customers: it ranks mostly by removal savings, so in tight-capacity instances it repeatedly removes cheap-to-move low-demand nodes and leaves the bin-packing-like capacity structure (and the long depot legs of eccentric instances) untouched. Testable claim: scoring removal priority as a multiplicative gate of (a) normalized removal savings, (b) demand-to-residual-load pressure of the node's route, and (c) a depot-distance gate applied only when the route is far-loaded, combined through a stagnation-driven rank power, will lower mean tour length on dev_24 below the current SBS 16.0496, with the gain concentrated on the tight-capacity and eccentric-depot subsets (predicting subset mean improvement >= 0.05 while uniform-demand/spatial-random subsets stay within noise).

next_search_advice.direction: Capacity-tightness-aware multiplicative gated rank-power ruin scoring (targeting the 'tight capacity' / eccentric-depot weak regime)
